title: Revisiting AdaGrad in Stochastic Convex Optimization: Last Iterates, High Probability, and Lower Bounds
summary: AdaGrad and AdaGrad-Norm are widely used adaptive methods, but their precise behavior in stochastic convex optimization remains less understood. We first show that AdaGrad-Norm and AdaGrad do not admit any universal \textbf{last-iterate} rate, even under sub-Gaussian noise and bounded iterates. We then prove that bounded variance alone is too weak: even with bounded iterates, it cannot yield \textbf{high-probability average-iterate} rates, and without bounded iterates it may not even guarantee convergence in expectation.
